A user has filed a support ticket reporting that their experience
with the service has degraded — requests feel slow or are failing
for them. The on-call team needs you to investigate.

Telemetry parquets are stored in: `.`
Available files: abnormal_metrics.parquet, abnormal_traces.parquet,
abnormal_logs.parquet, abnormal_metrics_histogram.parquet,
abnormal_metrics_sum.parquet, normal_metrics.parquet,
normal_traces.parquet, normal_logs.parquet.

Walk the telemetry to identify which endpoints / services are
actually affected, then determine the root cause(s) of the
degradation.

content.text: Key finding so far: in the abnormal period the `search` service emits no spans at all. Frontend's `search.Search/Nearby` calls fail in about 0.02 ms with 565 errors, and `/hotels` returns 500. Next I'll check logs and pod-level metrics for `search` and its callees.

content.text: The search pod's container cannot start (`exec: "search": executable file not found in $PATH`), so it crash-loops and never becomes ready. Its effect reaches frontend, which returns 500 on `/hotels`. I have enough to answer.

input.reflection: Single fault: search service pod (search-7d9cf4559d-ktsrp) crash-loops. Evidence: restarts climb 4->8 in abnormal (flat 3 in normal), ready=0 throughout, no CPU/memory samples, kubelet Failed event 'executable file not found in $PATH', BackOff x20. Search emits zero spans in abnormal (366 server spans normal). Frontend search.Search/Nearby client spans error in 0.02ms (565), and HTTP /hotels returns 500 (565) vs normal 499 OK. Geo/rate/reservation go silent downstream because search never calls them. Other services' restarts match normal baseline. Kind: pod_unavailable (stays down through window; equivalent to pod_failure). Propagation: search -> frontend.
